weakest_link: The overlap window. Line 1 is due end-2028 and the floating units 2028–31, so the bridge may earn only 0–2 years. Meanwhile about 80 MW of gensets plus about 200k m³ of corrected Arctic tankage (unpriced, roughly $150–250m+) are paid up front. It also depends on the all-season road being ready. On a winter road alone it needs 118–140 loads/day, which is not credible.
flip_test: The confirmed date of firm floating-unit power at Nagleynyn compared with line 1 mechanical completion, and whether the Pevek road is all-season by then. | If floating-unit power arrives less than about 9–12 months after line 1, the corrected margin (about $0.3–0.4bn/y at the base price, under $0.2bn at Cu $8k) no longer covers genset mobilisation and tank-farm capex, and "none" leads. The same happens if the road is winter-only in 2028–29.
